blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A singular subject requires a singular verb, while a plural subject requires a plural verb.
Indefinite pronouns such as 'each', 'every', 'either', and 'neither' take singular verbs.
With 'either...or' and 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it.
Collective nouns take a singular verb when acting as a unit, but a plural verb when members act individually.
Quantities representing distance, time, and money are treated as singular concepts.

blocks.content:
Subject–Verb Agreement means that the verb must match the subject in number and person.



Singular subject → singular verb

Plural subject → plural verb



Example:

• She writes daily.

• They write daily.



WHY THIS CHAPTER IS CRITICAL:

A large percentage of SSC error-detection questions are directly based on subject–verb agreement. If this topic becomes strong, grammar accuracy improves dramatically.

A singular subject takes a singular verb, and a plural subject takes a plural verb.



Singular:

The boy plays.



Plural:

The boys play.



IMPORTANT TIP:

Ignore extra words between subject and verb. Always identify the REAL subject.

When words like "of", "with", "along with", "together with", "in addition to" come after the subject, they DO NOT change the number.



Example:

The quality of the apples is good.



The teacher along with the students is attending.



Wrong:

The teacher along with the students are attending.

Two subjects joined by 'and' usually take a plural verb.



Ravi and Aman are playing.



EXCEPTION 1:

When both refer to the SAME person or idea → singular verb.



Bread and butter is my favorite breakfast.



EXCEPTION 2:

When preceded by "each" or "every" → singular verb.



Every boy and every girl is ready.

These always take singular verbs.



Each student is responsible.

Neither answer is correct.



Even when followed by plural nouns:

Each of the players is talented.

The verb agrees with the SUBJECT closest to it.



Either the teacher or the students are responsible.

Either the students or the teacher is responsible.



SSC frequently tests this proximity rule.

When the group acts as ONE → singular verb.



The team is winning.



When members act individually → plural verb.



The team are arguing among themselves.



Understand the LOGIC, not just the rule.

Always Singular:

everyone, someone, anyone, nobody, each, either, neither



Example:

Everyone is invited.



Plural:

few, many, several



Flexible:

all, some, none (depend on noun)

A number of → plural verb

The number of → singular verb



Example:

A number of students are absent.

The number of students is increasing.
10. NOUNS THAT LOOK PLURAL BUT ARE SINGULAR

Examples:

scissors

trousers

spectacles



Correct:

The scissors are sharp.



Use:

A pair of scissors is missing.

Titles of books, movies, and subjects take singular verbs.



"Gulliver's Travels" is an interesting novel.

When viewed as a single unit → singular verb.



Five kilometers is a long walk.

Ten years is a long time.

A gerund (-ing form) acting as a subject takes a singular verb.



Swimming is good exercise.

Reading improves knowledge.

When an infinitive acts as the subject → singular verb.



To err is human.

Although it sounds plural, it takes a singular verb.



More than one student has failed.

Structure:

One of the + plural noun + singular verb.



One of the players is injured.

In 'there is/are' constructions, the verb agrees with the REAL subject.



There is a book on the table.

There are many books on the table.

Verb depends on the noun after 'of'.



50% of the cake is eaten.

50% of the students are absent.

Verb depends on the noun.



A lot of water is wasted.

A lot of people are waiting.

items: 'A number of' takes a plural noun and a plural verb, whereas 'The number of' takes a singular verb.
'More than one' is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb.
Qualifying phrases introduced by 'as well as', 'together with', or 'along with' do not change the number of the main subject.
'One of the' is followed by a plural noun but takes a singular verb.

blocks.content:
Words like:

as well as

along with

together with

in addition to



DO NOT make the subject plural.



The captain, along with the players, is arriving.

1. Identify the real subject.

2. Ignore interrupting phrases.

3. Learn proximity rule.

4. Memorize indefinite pronouns.

5. Watch tricky expressions.

6. Understand collective noun logic.

Incorrect: Each of the students are ready.

Correct: Each of the students is ready.



Incorrect: Bread and butter are tasty.

Correct: Bread and butter is tasty.



Incorrect: More than one person are involved.

Correct: More than one person is involved.

Fill in the blanks:



1. Each of the players ___ selected. (is/are)

2. A number of candidates ___ absent.

3. Bread and butter ___ my favorite breakfast.

4. There ___ many reasons to celebrate.



Answers:

is, are, is, are

Subject–Verb Agreement is the backbone of grammatical correctness.



Key Takeaways:



• Match verb with the real subject.

• Learn special rules thoroughly.

• Focus on SSC trap patterns.

• Do not be misled by plural-looking words.
